web.name: Websites and web apps
web.title: Website and web application development
web.metaTitle: Website and Web Application Development | Ali Onar
web.metaDescription: Company websites, admin panels, quoting and ordering systems, B2B platforms. I build custom web software end to end, from analysis to launch.
web.lead: From company websites to admin panels, from quoting and ordering systems to B2B platforms, I build web software shaped around your business. Analysis, design, development and launch are handled by one person.

summary.for: Businesses that off-the-shelf tools do not fit and that want to run their processes their own way.
summary.deliver: A live website or application, an admin panel and a walkthrough for your team.
summary.how: Written scope and timeline, weekly demos, support after launch.

included.title: Company website
included.text: A fast site that explains your services and products, works well on phones and is easy for Google to read.

included.title: Admin panel
included.text: A panel designed around your work, where requests, quotes, orders, customers and payments live on one screen.

included.title: Quoting and ordering flows
included.text: Moving quotes, orders and paperwork that run on Excel or paper into a system you can track.

included.title: Integrations
included.text: Payment providers (iyzico, Param, Stripe), WhatsApp, SMS, email and Telegram notifications.

included.title: Multilingual setup
included.text: Language-specific pages and international search settings for companies selling abroad.

included.title: Hosting and maintenance
included.text: Server setup, domain and security settings, backups and updates after launch.

projects.note: Company website and the management panel behind it: service and quote requests, calendar, quotes and payments in one place.
Product and company website published in six languages, with dealer and service logins and service request flows.
Company website with service pages, a quick request flow and WhatsApp integration.

process.title: Intro call
process.text: I listen to what you need and how you work today. This call is free.

process.title: Analysis and written proposal
process.text: I prepare a detailed proposal covering scope, screens, timeline and payment plan.

process.title: Development with weekly demos
process.text: We review the working version every week, and your feedback shapes the following week.

process.title: Testing, launch and support
process.text: After testing I launch the product, walk your team through it and provide support afterwards.

faq.q: How long does a website or application take?
faq.a: It depends on the scope. I do not guess the timeline; I give it stage by stage in the proposal I prepare after the analysis.

faq.q: How is the price set?
faq.a: Scope sets the price: number of screens, integrations and content preparation. After the first call I send the scope, timeline and payment plan in writing, so you see what you pay for up front.

faq.q: Can you move our current site or Excel files into the new system?
faq.a: Yes. Existing content, product lists, customer records and Excel templates are migrated. We plan the switch together so it does not disrupt your work.

faq.q: Do you provide support after launch?
faq.a: Yes. I handle bug fixes, updates and new feature requests under a maintenance arrangement.

cta.title: Let's talk about your project
cta.text: Describe what you need in a few sentences and I will get back to you shortly to schedule an intro call.

included.title: Admin panel and metrics

faq.q: Can I take payments from Turkey and abroad?

faq.q: Will the foundation hold when the product grows?
faq.a: I set up the foundation for growth from day one and choose technologies by long-term total cost. The aim is that you do not have to rewrite the system when the number of users increases.

rescue.name: Unfinished projects
rescue.title: Finishing stalled software projects
rescue.metaTitle: Finishing Stalled Software Projects | Ali Onar
rescue.metaDescription: I take over software projects left behind by a previous team or generated with AI tools and stuck, fix the problems and bring them to launch.
rescue.lead: I take over projects left behind by a previous team or generated with AI tools and unable to move forward. I review where things stand, identify the problems, then finish the project and launch it.

summary.for: Businesses whose developer left, who never received the finished work, or who got stuck on a project started with AI.
summary.deliver: A written report on the current state, then a finished product running live.
summary.how: Review and report first, then a decision we make together, then staged delivery.

included.title: State review
included.text: I review the code, the database and the server, and report in writing what works and what is missing.

included.title: Continue or rewrite?
included.text: I recommend, with reasons, whether it costs less to build on the existing code or to rewrite the critical parts.

included.title: Bug and security fixes
included.text: I prioritise and fix critical issues such as sign-in, payments and data loss.

included.title: Completing what is missing
included.text: I finish half-built screens and flows and repair broken integrations.

included.title: Launch
included.text: I take the project live safely with server, domain, backup and monitoring in place.

included.title: Documentation
included.text: I document how the system works and how to run it, so the project does not depend on one person.

projects.note: I took over an unfinished, AI-generated codebase and brought it live, rebuilding the server side from scratch.
On a legal AI platform I took over, I improved answer quality and the membership and payment flows.
Starting from an AI-generated prototype, I rewrote the application to be ready for production.

process.title: Intro call
process.text: I listen to where the project stopped and what is hurting you most.

process.title: State review and report
process.text: With read access to the code and server I review the project and share my findings and the route I recommend in writing.

process.title: Staged completion
process.text: I fix the critical problems first, then complete the missing features with weekly demos.

process.title: Launch and handover
process.text: I launch the project, hand it over with its documentation and provide support afterwards.

faq.q: We cannot reach the previous developer. Can you still take over?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. If you have access to the source code, the server and the domain, I can review it. If access is missing, we work out together which accounts can be recovered and how.

faq.q: Does the project need to be rewritten?
faq.a: Not always. After the review I report, with reasons, whether continuing with the existing code or rewriting specific parts costs less; the decision is yours.

faq.q: Can a project we generated with AI tools go live?
faq.a: It can, but there are usually gaps in security, data structure and payments. I close those gaps and make the project ready for real users.

faq.q: How does the takeover start?
faq.a: I listen to the problem in the first call. Then, with read access to the code and server, I review the project and share my findings and the route I recommend in writing.

cta.title: Let's talk about where your project stands
cta.text: Describe where the project stopped in a few sentences and I will get back to you shortly about how we can move forward.

seo.name: SEO
seo.title: SEO and visibility on Google
seo.metaTitle: SEO and Visibility on Google | Ali Onar
seo.metaDescription: Technical SEO, keywords and page structure, local SEO and measurement. As a developer I implement the recommendations on the site myself.
seo.lead: I handle the full SEO work, from technical foundations to content structure, so your website shows up for what your customers search on Google. As a developer I do not leave recommendations in a report; I implement them on the site myself.

summary.for: Businesses whose customers search on Google but who trail competitors in the results.
summary.deliver: Technical fixes, page structure built around target keywords and regular progress reports.
summary.how: Analysis of the current state first, then implementation in priority order and regular measurement.

included.title: Technical SEO
included.text: Site speed, mobile friendliness, sitemap, redirects and the fixes that let Google read your pages correctly.

included.title: Keywords and page structure
included.text: I find the terms your customers really search for and plan the right page for each.

included.title: Local SEO
included.text: Visibility in city and region searches; Google Business Profile and local pages.

included.title: Content plan
included.text: A content plan for service pages and blog posts based on search intent.

included.title: Structured data
included.text: Schema.org markup for richer appearance in search results.

included.title: Measurement and reporting
included.text: Rankings, clicks and enquiries tracked with Search Console and Analytics; regular, readable reports.

projects.note: Technical and on-page SEO targeting the first page for chiller service searches in the Marmara region.
The website of a fitness app reaching 60,000+ monthly web visitors.
An SEO-focused page structure built for wholesale pickle and product-level searches.

process.title: Current state analysis
process.text: I review your site, your competitors and your Search Console data to find where you are losing ground.

process.title: Priority plan
process.text: I put the fixes with the most impact and the target keywords in order.

process.title: Implementation
process.text: I apply the technical fixes, page structure and content changes on the site myself.

process.title: Measurement and improvement
process.text: I report rankings, clicks and incoming enquiries regularly and continue according to the plan.

faq.q: When do SEO results show?
faq.a: It depends on how competitive the keyword is and where the site stands today. Technical fixes usually show within weeks; ranking gains on competitive keywords take months. I do not promise a date or a position; I show progress with data.

faq.q: You did not build our site. Can you still work on it?
faq.a: Yes. I review your current setup and work out what can be done. If the platform itself blocks your goals, I say so with reasons.

faq.q: SEO or Google Ads?
faq.a: They complement each other. Ads bring enquiries immediately but stop when the budget ends; SEO takes longer but lasts. For most businesses the right route is to start with ads and grow SEO in parallel.

faq.q: What will I see in the reports?
faq.a: Where you rank for which keyword, how many people came from Google and how many of those visits turned into enquiries. I report business results rather than technical terms.

cta.title: Let's look at your site together
cta.text: Send your site address and the searches you care about, and I will get back to you shortly with a first assessment.

ads.name: Google Ads management
ads.title: Google Ads management
ads.metaDescription: Google Ads account setup, conversion tracking, landing pages and regular optimisation. I manage the ad, the page and the measurement together.
ads.lead: I set up and manage your Google Ads account so you appear at the right moment for people searching for your service. Because I also build the landing page and the conversion tracking myself, you see clearly what your budget turns into.

summary.for: Businesses that want enquiries from Google, or that advertise but cannot see what they get for it.
summary.deliver: An ad account with working measurement, landing pages, regular optimisation and reports.
summary.how: Account and measurement audit first, then campaign setup and regular optimisation.

included.title: Account and campaign setup
included.text: Search campaigns, ad groups and ad copy built around your services and service area.

included.title: Conversion tracking
included.text: I measure form, phone and WhatsApp clicks, or your real goal such as sign-ups, so you see which keyword brings enquiries.

included.title: Keyword and negative keyword management
included.text: I cut budget going to irrelevant searches and steer spending to the keywords that bring enquiries.

included.title: Landing pages
included.text: I prepare fast pages that match your ad groups and are arranged to collect enquiries.

included.title: Bid and budget optimisation
included.text: I update the bid strategy and budget split regularly based on the data.

included.title: Reporting
included.text: I share spend, clicks, number of enquiries and cost per enquiry in a plain report.

process.title: Account and measurement audit
process.text: If you already have an account, I check where the budget goes and whether measurement works correctly.

process.title: Campaign and page setup
process.text: I set up the campaigns, ad copy, conversion tracking and the pages the ads lead to.

process.title: Regular optimisation
process.text: I update search terms, bids and ad copy regularly based on the data.

process.title: Report and plan
process.text: I share the results in a plain report and we set the plan for the next period together.

faq.q: How much ad budget do we need?
faq.a: It depends on the sector, the city and how competitive your keywords are. After the first call I estimate costs per keyword, and I recommend starting with a small budget and raising it as data comes in.

faq.q: When do ads start to work?
faq.a: Ads begin to show the day they go live. Sound decisions need a few weeks of data; during that time I adjust keywords and ad copy based on what the data shows.

faq.q: Can you take over our existing ad account?
faq.a: Yes. I audit the account first and report where the budget goes and whether measurement works; then I apply the fixes.

faq.q: What if our site is not suitable for ads?
faq.a: If the page an ad leads to is not built to collect enquiries, the budget is wasted. Where needed I rework the existing page or prepare separate pages for the ads.

cta.title: Let's look at your ad account together
cta.text: Send your site address and what you expect from ads, and I will get back to you shortly with a first assessment.

process.title: Intro call
process.text: I listen to the decision in front of you and the options you have.

process.title: Review
process.text: Code, a proposal, servers or process: I review the material the question calls for.

process.title: Written assessment
process.text: I report the findings, the risks and the route I recommend in plain language.

process.title: Support in applying it
process.text: If you wish, I accompany your team or the company you work with while the decision is applied.

faq.q: I am not technical. Will I understand the report?
faq.a: Yes. I write the assessment in terms of cost, risk and time rather than technical jargon, and we can go through it together on a call.

faq.q: We have a quote from another company. Can you stay impartial?
faq.a: Yes. In consulting my aim is not to win the work but to help you make the right decision; I assess only the proposal itself.

faq.q: Do you work one-off or ongoing?
faq.a: Both are possible. I can do a one-off review for a single decision or stay alongside you regularly through a project.

faq.q: What access do you need for a code review?
faq.a: Read access to the source code, and preferably to the server, is enough.

cta.title: Let's weigh your decision together
